answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region, so the one action that actually moves customer writes off the degraded primary is regional failover. memory_b2 is the closest prior: latency recovered in minutes after a clean traffic shift. Cause is not unique—the 2h-old release could be at fault (memory_b1), but that case was an error spike, not write latency, and a write-path rollback at settlement peak is more likely to drop or dual-version in-flight writes. memory_b5 only helps if reads/reports are saturating the primary; writes would remain on the sick primary. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) fail fast and would shed customer writes, which violates the objective. Failover during peak settlement can still jeopardize in-flight settlement value, so that downstream risk is flagged. Verifying memory_b2 for write-loss/replication caveats before treating the March outcome as fully transferable.
